review.summary: Critique of the mechanotransduction, cell recovery rate, and fixed-point solver in the oxidative tensegrity model. The analysis reveals that the reported baseline cell recovery rate (0.166 /h) is a hardcoded artifact of the assumed myosin turnover timescale (tau_M = 6.0 h). Furthermore, the reduction in recovery rate in soft matrices reflects standard linear feedback gain from Hill function slopes rather than critical slowing down near a true bifurcation, and finite-difference Jacobians suffer from Monte Carlo clutch noise.

findings.title: Fixed-point iteration loop in CellModel lacks residual convergence check
findings.evidence: CellModel.steady_state executes a fixed loop of 6 damped iterations without evaluating fixed-point residual |M_{k+1} - M_k| or checking tolerance.
findings.implication: If 6 iterations fail to converge for stiff or non-linear matrix regimes, downstream steady-state YAP, contractility, and traction values are non-equilibrium numerical artifacts.
findings.recommended_check: Replace the fixed iteration loop with an explicit residual convergence check while np.max(np.abs(M_next - M)) > 1e-5 and assert convergence.

findings.title: Baseline recovery rate of 0.166 /h is an artifact of hardcoded myosin turnover timescale tau_M = 6 h
findings.evidence: CellParams sets tau_M = 6.0 h, giving uncoupled eigenvalue -1/tau_M = -0.1666 /h. When dY/dM = 0, the Jacobian eigenvalues are -1/tau_Y = -2.0 /h and -1/tau_M = -0.1666 /h.
findings.implication: The baseline recovery rate of 0.166 /h cited throughout the project is not an emergent property of network-cell mechanotransduction, but an exact reproduction of the user-assigned parameter 1/tau_M.
findings.recommended_check: Vary tau_M systematically (e.g., 1 h to 24 h) to verify that baseline recovery rate scales inversely with tau_M.

findings.title: Finite-difference Jacobian calculation with single clutch seed introduces stochastic derivative noise
findings.evidence: recovery_rate evaluates dY/dM using a central finite difference step dM = 0.15 on stochastic motor-clutch runs. In results/cpu32/cell.csv, dY/dM fluctuates into negative values (-0.0025, -0.0019) on stiff matrices.
findings.implication: Single-seed Monte Carlo clutch noise corrupts the local derivative dY/dM, producing unphysical negative feedback estimates and noisy eigenvalue shifts.
findings.recommended_check: Average Y(M) over an ensemble of random clutch seeds before evaluating finite differences, or fit a smooth surrogate curve Y(M).

findings.title: Absence of true bifurcation: feedback gain beta * dY/dM remains far below unity
findings.evidence: The Jacobian determinant is (1 - beta * dY/dM) / (tau_Y * tau_M). Across cell.csv, maximum dY/dM is ~0.155, giving maximum loop gain beta * dY/dM = 1.5 * 0.155 = 0.2325, far below 1.0.
findings.implication: The modest drop in recovery rate from 0.166 /h to 0.12-0.14 /h is standard feedback-induced eigenvalue shifting along the Hill curve slope, not critical slowing down approaching a tipping point or bifurcation.
findings.recommended_check: Test whether increasing beta above 1 / (dY/dM)_{max} ~ 6.5 induces a true saddle-node bifurcation where the recovery rate vanishes.

findings.title: Traction-state entropy and entropy production are passive monotonic proxies of matrix stiffness
findings.evidence: Traction entropy H is derived from force histograms, and entropy production is computed as motor work plus slip power divided by k_B T, both scaling strictly with matrix Young's modulus E.
findings.implication: The entropy metrics provide no independent thermodynamic state information beyond re-stating substrate stiffness and motor stall loading.
findings.recommended_check: Evaluate whether H or entropy production yield non-trivial variation when matrix stiffness E is held constant while varying clutch parameters.

review.strongest_surviving_claim: Oxidative crosslinking increases linear shear modulus and flattens strain-stiffening non-linearity in sub-isostatic collagen networks, driving motor-clutch adhesions into high-traction, YAP-saturated regimes.
review.decisive_next_experiment: Longitudinal microfluidic tracking of individual age-matched C. elegans (e.g., day-5 adults): apply a transient mechanical pressure pulse, time the individual return of YAP-1::GFP nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio to baseline (tau_rec), and record individual time-to-death without intervention to test whether tau_rec predicts remaining lifespan independently of chronological age.
